verdict.rationale: Gitea documents its own automation surfaces: an official CLI (tea), a Go SDK, an action runner for Gitea Actions, GitHub Actions-compatible YAML workflows, and a versioned /api/v1 REST API with a built-in OpenAPI/Swagger document. Together these show the product can be driven programmatically and in CI pipelines. The evidence does not show tea or the API actually running non-interactively in CI (token-based auth for pipelines, scripted flags, machine-readable output), and there is no hands-on corroboration, so coverage is partial. Missing for 10: documented non-interactive/headless CLI usage in CI, a CI authentication pattern for tea, machine-readable CLI output, and independent hands-on corroboration of headless automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: We provide an official go-sdk, a CLI tool called tea and an action runner for Gitea Action.
Gitea Actions supports CI/CD functionality, compatible with GitHub Actions. Users can write workflows in familiar YAML format and reuse a variety of existing Actions plugins.
The OpenAPI document is at: https://gitea.your.host/swagger.v1.json
